newsitem.title: POLAND: Canada says its Polish investment to double in '97.
newsitem.headline: Canada says its Polish investment to double in '97.

text.p: Canada wants Poland to become its foothold for trade expansion in central and eastern Europe and will likely double its investment here next year, Canadian Foreign Trade Minister Arthur Eggleton said on Tuesday.

"For Canada, Poland is already its No. 1 market in central Europe and I think it can be the gateway for Canadian business into the countries of CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement)," Eggleton told a news conference.
Apart from Poland, CEFTA groups other former Soviet bloc countries -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia. Several countries want to join the free trade pact.

Eggleton, who led a delegation of 30 Canadian business executives during his two-day visit ending on Tuesday, said Canadian firms, which have so far invested $80 million in Poland, are likely to double the sum by the end of 1997.

"I predict that over the next year the amount of Canadian investment in Poland will double," he said, adding new projects are likely to be launched in telecommunications, agriculture, construction and environmental technology.
He said he had discussed prospects of increasing wheat exports to Poland with Polish Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski but that it was too early to disclose any details.
Eggleton also said that with his Polish counterpart Janusz Kaczurba he discussed closer cooperation between Polish and Canadian export guaranteeing bodies to boost trade.
According to the Polish government, mutual trade increased by 32 percent to $178 million last year compared with 1994 and Poland had a $15 million deficit.
